description:
PDF editor for Windows that also reads EPUB and DjVu. No account, no subscription, no telemetry.

KillerPDF is a free, open-source PDF editor for Windows. View, annotate, edit text and paragraphs, OCR, merge, split, sign and verify signatures, fill and build forms, redact, protect, compare, print and flatten PDFs, export them to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML or Markdown, read EPUB books and DjVu scans and convert them to PDF, and repeat the work with macros, watched folders and the command line, all without an Adobe subscription. WinGet installs machine-wide; the downloadable installer also supports per-user installation, and a separate portable build is available. Document processing stays on your computer, with no account, no subscription, and no telemetry. Open source under GPLv3.
1.9.4 is a bugfix release: Rasterize Region removes the text inside the box, text can be selected before it is highlighted, printing a turned page no longer crashes, and the tool menu floats over the page again, with a switch to dock it.

### Fixed

- Printing a page that turns to fit the sheet no longer crashes with "The calling thread cannot access this object because a different thread owns it." (#492)
- Rasterize Region removes the text inside the box, so it can no longer be searched, selected or copied from under the image. A letter that crosses the box's edge stays, so its outside half is still drawn. On a tagged PDF the image keeps the removed words as alternative text for screen readers, and the dialog points to Redact for hiding text. (#369)
- Rotating a page turns everything on it: pictures, signatures and text boxes now turn with the page and stay on the content they were placed on, as highlights, drawings and measurements already did.
- A picture cut or copied from a page shown turned is pasted and saved turned the same way, instead of upright and running past the page.
- Text edits on scans (#467): copying the replacement text or its cover copies the whole object, so a paste brings both; with the text box locked and the cover free, the cover moves on its own with the mouse and the arrow keys; after a click on a layer's eye or hand, the arrow keys move the selection instead of scrolling the page; and a hidden replacement keeps a faint dashed outline on screen that can be clicked to show it again.
- Page thumbnails show unsaved edits: pasted pictures, signatures, text boxes, highlights, covers, drawings and measurements appear on a page's thumbnail as soon as they are placed, moved or removed, instead of only after saving.
- The tool menu floats over the top edge of the page area again by default, as it did before 1.9.3, so choosing a tool no longer moves the page down. Drag it by its grip or empty space to slide it along the edge, and double-click it to minimize it to a strip. (#485)
- Choosing Highlight, Underline or Strikethrough with text already selected marks that text instead of clearing the selection, and while one of those tools is on, the pointer is an I-beam over text and a cross elsewhere. (#485)
- In 98SE, the window's close X, minimize line and maximize box are full size again on the Win98-sized caption buttons, and every close button, in dialogs and on cards too, draws Win98's pixel X instead of a smoothed font glyph.
- In 98SE, the About card's right and bottom edges end in Win98's black line instead of a light gray stripe.
- About's settings keep even spacing in each column when a label wraps, Clear all Data sits in the bottom-right corner, and the card's top margin matches its sides.

### Changed

- The replacement-text blur slider is logarithmic: light blur takes most of its travel and the strongest blur the last stretch. (#467)
- About no longer shows a color management status line under the version. The version still opens the release notes.
- Right-clicking a picture opens a picture card instead of a three-item menu. It names the picture with its size in pixels and its page, and holds Copy, Cut and Delete as buttons. A pasted picture also gets Raise, Lower, Rotate CCW, Upside Down and Rotate CW, which turn it in place.

### Added

- Docked Tool Menu and Floating Tool Menu choose whether the tool menu sits above the page or floats over its top edge. They are on the toolbar's right-click menu and a right-click on the tool menu itself, with a small icon of each layout, and Alt+B switches between them. (#485)
- Save Picture As on the picture card writes a picture to its own file. A pasted picture keeps its original file type byte for byte, and a picture that is part of the page is saved as a PNG at its own resolution.
- Replace Picture on a pasted picture's card swaps in another image file in the same spot and width.
